pages.text: The Hawk-Dove game: two meet over a prize V. A hawk fights; a dove shares with another dove and backs down from a hawk. Two hawks fight, one wins V and the loser pays an injury C. When a share p of the population are hawks, a hawk earns p(V − C)/2 + (1 − p)V and a dove (1 − p)V/2. Their difference, (V − pC)/2, is zero only at p = V/C: the stable mix.
$(thing)Set$(): Hawk share, Rounds.$(br2)$(thing)Disturbance$(): Uneven prizes: V varies by ±2%·d.
$(thing)Limits$(): none beyond the recipe windows.$(br2)$(thing)Rate$(): Fewer rounds are faster.
